memories.content: Keep the total, major cost categories, and one-line estimate basis in the main text so the resource argument can be understood without leaving the proposal.
Place each major cost beside the activity or deliverable it enables in the main text.
State the quantity and unit-rate basis for each major cost in the same paragraph that requests it.
Readers may question a proposed priority when its cost cannot be checked on the same page as the claimed benefit.
Update the cost sentence whenever the related activity changes so the narrative and requested amount cannot drift apart.
Accept a denser main-text paragraph when the estimate basis is essential to deciding whether the request is proportionate.
The user tends to revise the work plan but forget a detached budget table unless the key amount is repeated beside the activity.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate proposal concerns: the reference frame focuses on making costs visible, checkable, and synchronized with activities, while the compared frame sets participant-protection requirements for field user studies. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other’s claims.

relations.reason: This is a one-sided cost-transparency requirement with no operational counterpart in the participant-protection frame.
relations.summary: Major cost information and its quantity-and-rate estimate basis should appear in the proposal’s main text where the request is made.

relations.reason: The memories express the same underlying requirement to connect costs visibly to their justification; the compared frame does not address proposal cost placement.
relations.summary: Major costs should be presented beside the activities or benefits they enable so readers can check the resource argument on the same page.

relations.reason: The prescriptive update rule and observed revision failure describe one underlying drift-prevention need absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Key amounts should remain beside and synchronized with their activities when the work plan changes.

relations.reason: This is an independent presentation tradeoff found only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: A denser main-text paragraph is acceptable when estimate detail is necessary to judge whether a request is proportionate.

relations.reason: The operational requirement and reviewer check restate one task-level ethics criterion with no cost-presentation counterpart.
relations.summary: Anticipated participant burden and mitigation strategies should correspond for every field user study task.

relations.reason: These memories split the necessary content and delivery aspects of one accessibility plan, which appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A field user study should specify both the accommodations participants need and how those accommodations will be provided.

relations.reason: This independent data-protection requirement has no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers should be separated from research data immediately upon collection using a described procedure.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful equipment-access requirement present only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Equipment available for loan to participants who lack required gear should be listed.

relations.reason: This distinct equipment-return requirement is not stated in the reference frame.
relations.summary: The procedure for participants to return loaned equipment should be described.

relations.reason: The operational safeguard and its withdrawal-risk rationale express one underlying requirement absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Field tasks should have a safe existing-work alternative that participants can resume if they withdraw from research.

relations.reason: This independent non-retaliation protection appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Organizational members who decline research participation should face no disadvantage in task assignment or performance evaluation.

relations.reason: This is a distinct observed assessment risk with no corresponding claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Burden assessment should not infer low burden from a short session while overlooking work interruption and exposure to a manager.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers task-specific burden mitigation, accessibility, data separation, equipment logistics, safe withdrawal, non-retaliation, and risks of underestimating workplace disruption or managerial exposure.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame requires decision-relevant costs and estimate bases in the main narrative, linked to activities and kept synchronized despite revisions, even when this increases textual density.
